status_summary: Anadolu reported on 2025-02-19, relaying the Washington Post, that the US had halted funding for Palestinian Authority security forces as part of the broader foreign aid freeze, with some training programs cancelled. On 2025-07-31 State announced visa sanctions on PA officials and PLO members after reporting to Congress that both were out of compliance with commitments under two statutes, and on 2025-08-29 it announced it would deny visas to the PA president and about 80 other PA officials ahead of the UN General Assembly. The visa measures restrict travel rather than funds. No source found shows a formal, comprehensive cutoff of all PA funds or a provision specific to the PA in the FY2026 appropriations law.

timeline.event: The Washington Post, as relayed by Anadolu, reported the US had halted funding for Palestinian Authority security forces as part of the foreign aid freeze.

title: Defund the Palestinian Authority
uncertainties: The February 2025 halt is a secondhand report of a Washington Post story, with no dollar amount and no State document read. The July 2025 measures rest on the State media note as republished by GlobalSecurity, since state.gov itself was not read. The FY2026 appropriations law (Public Law 119-75) was not read for Palestinian Authority provisions; the advocacy summary listed in sources predates enactment and does not mention the PA. Direct US economic aid to the PA was already restricted by earlier statutes that were not reviewed here, so the baseline is unclear. Inference: progress is set at 30 because the only funding step found is a reported halt of security assistance under a general freeze, while the other actions found are visa measures.
